traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and explicit requirements in `docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md` are implemented and covered by tests and documentation:
- **Rule naming & aliasing (REQ-RULE-NAME)**: `traceability/prefer-supports-annotation` is exposed as the primary rule name, with `traceability/prefer-implements-annotation` wired as a deprecated alias (`src/index.ts`), and tests assert both names are available and behave identically. - **Optional warning & multi-story detection (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT)**: Rule only reports on legacy `@story`+`@req` blocks and multi-story/mixed cases, with precise messages matching the story, and is disabled by default in presets; tests verify this behavior. - **Auto-fix & single-story conversion (REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT)**: Implementation provides a conservative auto-fix that rewrites eligible single-story blocks to a single `@supports` line while preserving comment structure and bailing out on complex/ambiguous patterns; unit tests validate single-REQ and multi-REQ conversions and no-fix behavior for complex cases. - **Configurable enforcement (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY)**: The rule uses standard ESLint severities (`off`/`warn`/`error`), is not included in built-in presets by default, and tests confirm both the primary and alias keys can be configured with different severities. - **Backward compatibility & validation (REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION, Both Formats Valid)**: Valid test cases prove that comments containing only `@story`, only `@req`, only `@supports`, or certain mixed-but-non-target patterns are ignored by this rule, ensuring legacy annotations remain valid when the rule is disabled or not configured. - **Documentation (Documentation acceptance criterion)**: A dedicated rule doc and the migration guide explain the rule’s purpose, configuration, auto-fix behavior, and limitations with examples, matching the story’s examples and configuration guidance.
The full Jest suite (including all tests for this story) passes, providing concrete verification that 010.3’s behavior works as specified. Therefore this story is fully implemented.
